description:
General notes page: a text-only sheet with a bordered frame and the heading 'General Notes' followed by ten numbered notes. No drawings, dimensions or tables appear on this sheet. The title block reads City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Roadside Freeway Guide Signing, Drawing No. S-418.5, sheet 2 of 9.

Notes content: Notes 1 and 2 cover where roadside freeway guide signing is used and how it is mounted. Notes 3 to 6 cover the three sign types (Lane Assignment, Action, Advance) and where freeway names are allowed, each referring to the lettered sign formats (Signs A through Z) drawn on the following sheets. Notes 7 to 10 cover lettering and layout of the sign text and when the dual direction Action format may be used.
notes:
1. See S-418.6 regarding the use of overhead versus roadside freeway guide signs. Use roadside freeway guide signing where access to the freeway is provided only by the right lane, where overhead signing may not be feasible or as interim signing until overhead signing can be installed.
2. See S-476.1 regarding mounting of roadside freeway guide signing. 4'x8', 5'x6', 4'x6' and 3'x8' signs require dual posts, while 3'x6' signs may be installed on an electrolier or single post. Signs up to 10 square feet (sq-ft) may be installed on steel electroliers within concrete sidewalks.
3. Lane Assignment freeway guide signs on multilane cross streets that have access to freeways are required per Section 2D.45 of the California MUTCD. Where roadside signs are to be used, apply the appropriate formats as shown in Signs B, C, F, G, I, L, R, S, W and X.
4. Action freeway guide signs are an essential follow-up to Lane Assignment freeway guide signs for assisting motorists in accessing the desired directions to freeways. Where roadside signs are to be used, apply the appropriate formats as shown in Signs D, H, J, K, M, N, O, P, T, U, Y and Z. They should be placed 100' to 200' in advance of the turn. See Note 9.
5. Advance freeway guide signs are necessary in advance of a pair of roadside Lane Assignment freeway guide signs in order to advise motorists early-on that both directions of the freeway are accessible. See the appropriate formats in Signs A, E, Q and V.
6. Freeway names are to be used only on the Advance sign or Lane Assignment sign (if an Advance sign is not appropriate) only where the on-ramps are within one mile of a freeway-to-freeway interchange, as shown in Signs A and E.
7. Where a long freeway name does not fit within the 8' wide format, as shown in Sign A, then Series C upper and lower case letters may be used. Where the freeway name and the word "Fwy" can fit on the first line then the freeway shield shall be shown alone on the second line.
8. The first capital letter of the cardinal direction is larger so as to provide improved recognition.
9. The dual direction Action freeway guide sign format as shown in Signs D and H versus the split directional formats as shown in Signs J, K, M, O, T, U, Y and Z is to be used only when physical constraints preclude effective placement of split signs.
10. The text on each line is to be centered.
title: Roadside Freeway Guide Signing - General Notes
summary: General notes for roadside (ground-mounted) freeway guide signs on cross streets that lead to freeways. They say when roadside signs are used instead of overhead signs, how large signs are mounted, and which lettered formats apply to Lane Assignment, Action and Advance signs. They also set rules for freeway names, cardinal direction lettering, centered text and the dual direction format.

The shaft is 3 9/16 in. tall and 2 3/4 in. is dimensioned at the shaft opening where it meets the head, with a 7/8 in. barb offset at the back of the head. Corner radius R = 5/8 in.

description:

A freeway runs vertically down the sheet, labeled 'Freeway' near the middle and 'Metropoliton' (as spelled on the sheet) lower down, with break lines (squiggles) showing it continues beyond the sheet. A California route shield marked 28 sits on the freeway at the top. A second, horizontal freeway labeled 'Urban Freeway' with an Interstate 205 shield crosses the bottom of the sheet and meets the vertical freeway at a four-level stack interchange (freeway-to-freeway). Three cross streets (two-way streets drawn as a pair of lines) cross the vertical freeway above the stack, each with ramps, and these show where each lettered sign (A through Z) is located. Each sign location is a dot with its letter beside it.

Bottom cross street (nearest the stack interchange, a diamond interchange with ramps on both sides): signs E, F, G, H on the left approach and signs A, B, C, D on the right approach. On the right approach, reading from the farthest sign toward the freeway, A to B is 400' min., B to C is 300' min. and C to D is 300' min. The overall run from A to D is dimensioned 1000'~1500' (1000 to 1500 feet). On the left approach E to F is 400' min., F to G is 300' min. and G to H is 300' min., with an overall dimension of 1000'~1500'. Per the sheet's own layout, A and E are the Advance signs at the far end, with the Lane Assignment and Action signs closer to the ramps.

description: Text-only sheet titled 'Application of Overhead Guide Signs', sheet 2 of 16 of drawing S-418.6 (City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Overhead Guide Signing, drawn by M.T.). It has a General paragraph with a bullet list of seven situations where overhead guide signs should generally be provided, followed by seven short sections, one per situation, each saying why overhead signs are desirable and which lettered sign sheets in the set apply. There are no drawings, dimensions or tables.
notes:
APPLICATION OF OVERHEAD GUIDE SIGNS
General: These signs are desirable to provide a high degree of visibility to forewarn and direct motorists on multi-lane approaches of roadway access or lane assignment conditions that generally cannot be anticipated. Situations where overhead signs generally should be provided include: divergent arterial roadways; skewed arterial approaches; unshadowed left-turn lanes; arterial grade separations, especially those which involve freeways; priority lanes, such as bus and/or carpool lanes; street name changes; end of one-way operation. While overhead signing should be used for the above situations, extenuating circumstances occasionally may suggest an alternative. Accordingly, roadside signing shall be used in the above situations where overhead signing is not used.
Divergent Arterial Roadways: Overhead signs are desirable because motorists cannot otherwise anticipate lane assignment and street name changes at the divergence. Where the intersecting street is not an arterial street and no lanes are entrapped onto it then overhead signing is not required. Also, where one of the arterial roadways has no change in horizontal alignment nor name and has no lanes that are entrapped onto the intersecting arterial roadway then no divergence exists and thus overhead signing is not required. See Signs A and B with related notes.
Skewed Arterial Approaches: Overhead signs are desirable because the deviation from right angles formed between the intersection legs can result in lane assignment ambiguity. See Signs C and D with related notes.
Unshadowed Left-Turn Lanes: Overhead signs are desirable on two-way streets so that motorists will readily recognize that the lane is entrapped and that there may be opposing traffic in the lane downstream. If there is a raised median then ground-mounted signing in the median may be adequate. See Signs B, C and D that display R3-5 signs with related notes and Signs S and U.
Arterial Grade Separations: Overhead signs are desirable because motorists cannot otherwise anticipate whether the connecting ramp configuration is on the left or right of the arterial approach. "Action" overhead signs show the immediate left-turn or divergent move necessary for access to the grade-separated facility. If there is a raised median then ground-mounted signing in the median may be adequate. "Action" overhead signs are not necessary for right turns or right-divergent moves, since "Lane Assignment" signs will direct motorists to the right lane(s) from where they can readily read roadside signing. See Signs E, F, G, H, H-Alternate, I, I-Alternate with related notes. "Lane Assignment" signs forewarn motorists as to which lanes of a multi-lane approach provide on-ramp access. Section 2D.45 of the California MUTCD requires "Lane Assignment" signs on multi-lane approaches to freeways. See Signs J, K, L, M and N with related notes.
Priority Lanes: Overhead signs are desirable for this rare regulatory condition which cannot otherwise be anticipated. See Signs O, P and Q with related notes.
Street Name Changes: Overhead signs are desirable at selected non-divergent locations and major junctions to advise motorists of the change in route name. Selected locations would be near regionally-significant activity centers. See Sign R.
End of One-Way Operation: Overhead signs are desirable so that motorists in the opposing direction (on the two-way leg of the intersection) may readily recognize that they must turn left and/or right. See Signs S, T and U.
title: Application of Overhead Guide Signs
summary: Explains when overhead guide signs should be used on multi-lane approaches: divergent and skewed arterials, unshadowed left-turn lanes, arterial grade separations, priority lanes, street name changes and the end of one-way operation. Where overhead signing is not used, roadside signing is required. Each situation points to the lettered sign sheets that follow.

description: Text-only sheet titled 'Overhead Sign Format Details', sheet 3 of 16 of drawing S-418.6 (City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Overhead Guide Signing, drawn by M.T.). It has four headed sections: Legend Size (minimum letter heights, letter series, supplemental wording, lane assignment wording, cardinal directions, spacing and line widths), Sign Size, Sign Structure (fabrication and support references) and Sign Retroreflectivity Material (a list of sheeting types by color). There are no drawings or tables.
notes:
OVERHEAD SIGN FORMAT DETAILS
Legend Size: The minimum size of letters on overhead signs is 8 inches upper case and 6 inches lower case. On streets with three or more approach lanes or with a posted speed limit of 40 miles per hour or greater 10.67 inch upper case and 8 inch lower case letters should be used.
Series E letter widths should be used, but in constrained situations Series C letter widths may be used.
Supplemental or clarifying wording on regulatory and guide signs (such as "ONTO BEVERLY DR", "200 FT" or "3 OR MORE") shall be 6 inch series D capital letters and numbers.
Lane Assignment wording ("RIGHT LANE", etc) shall be 6 inch Series D capital letters.
Cardinal directions shall have the first letter (N, S, E, W) larger so as to improve cardinal recognition. Where the general legend is 10.67 inches upper case and 8 inches lower case the cardinal direction should have 10 inch and 8 inch Series D letters. Where the general legend is 8 inches upper case and 6 inches lower case the cardinal direction should have 8 inch and 6 inch Series D letters.
The size of horizontal and vertical spacing should be equal to the height of the upper case letter. In constrained formats a minimum of one-half of these dimensions may be used. Division and border lines should be 1-1/2 inches wide.
See Sheets 4 and 5 for the sizes of arrows, route shields, and W61B(CA) and W61F(CA) signs.
Sign Size: The size of the sign is governed by the size of its elements. Sign software programs should be used to determine overall sign size.
Sign Structure: Fabrication of the sign from laminated, honeycomb panels using aluminum framing is shown in S-45.0. Cantilevered sign supports are shown in S92.2, S92.3, S98.0 and Plans S40N, S40P and S40Q of the State of California, Standard Plans.
Sign Retroreflectivity Material:
White Legend: Diamond (DG III) or Type VIII
Black Legend: Non-reflective Vinyl
Red legend: EC Film
Green Background: Type III
White Background: Type III
Yellow Background: Type III
All signs are to have match component UV/Anti Graffiti film.
title: Overhead Sign Format Details
summary: Sets legend sizes for overhead guide signs: 8 in. upper case and 6 in. lower case minimum, or 10.67 in. and 8 in. on streets with three or more approach lanes or speeds of 40 mph or more. It also covers letter series, supplemental wording, cardinal directions, spacing, sign structure references and retroreflective sheeting types by color.

The head is 11 1/4 in. tall and 7 1/4 in. wide to the left of the shaft. The shaft is 3 1/2 in. wide and the bend has a 4 in. radius. A 7/8 in. head offset is shown. Radius R = 5/8 in.

Down Vertical Arrow: a downward-pointing arrow. Overall width 24 in., overall height 16 1/2 in. and head height 12 in. The shaft stub is 5 in. wide and projects above the head, with a 2 in. dimension at the head. 3/4 in. dimensions mark the head corner offsets at each side.

Diagrammatic Arrows: four arrows. (1) A straight through arrow: head 9 in. wide (typ.), head height 7 3/4 in. (typ.), overall height 34 1/4 in. (typ.), shaft width 3 3/4 in. (typ.). (2) A through arrow with a left-curving branch: 19 in. (typ.) horizontal extent of the branch with a 21 5/8 in. (typ.) radius. (3) A through arrow with a right-curving branch: 27 1/2 in. (typ.) vertical extent of the branch. (4) A two-way split arrow (Y shape) with two curved branches pointing up-left and up-right, 34 3/4 in. (typ.) overall width.
notes: Arrow labels: One Line; Two Line; Advance Arrow; Down Vertical Arrow; Diagrammatic Arrows. Typical (typ.) dimensions apply to all diagrammatic arrows. Corner radii: R = 13/16 in. for the One Line and Two Line arrows, R = 5/8 in. for the Advance Arrow. No numbered notes on this sheet.
title: Arrow Styles and Specifications
summary: Full-size dimensioned outlines for the arrows used on overhead guide signs: One Line, Two Line, Advance, Down Vertical and four diagrammatic arrows (through, through with left branch, through with right branch, and a split Y). Overall sizes, head widths, shaft widths and radii are given in inches.

description:
Route Shield Sizes: five shield outlines with dimensions. U.S. route shield (example 101): 28 in. wide by 24 in. tall with 10 in. numerals. California route shield (example 27, 1 or 2 digits): 28 in. wide by 25 in. tall with 10 in. numerals. Interstate shield (example INTERSTATE 5, 1 or 2 digits): 24 in. wide by 24 in. tall with 10 in. numerals below the INTERSTATE band. California route shield (example 134, 3 digits): 32 in. wide with 10 in. numerals (its height is not dimensioned). Interstate shield (example INTERSTATE 405, 3 digits): 30 in. wide by 25 in. tall with 8 in. numerals.

W 61(CA) Signs: two rectangular signs with rounded corners and the word ONLY in 10 in. letters. The W61F(CA) sign is 84 in. wide by 20 in. tall, with ONLY at the left and a Down Vertical Arrow at the right (labeled on the sheet). The W61B(CA) sign is 44 in. wide by 20 in. tall with the word ONLY alone. Both are labeled 'Yellow or White Background as per Note 4' (Note 4 is on another sheet of this set). Sheet 5 of 16 of S-418.6.
notes: Route Shield Sizes captions: 1 or 2 digits; 3 digits. Labels: INTERSTATE 5; INTERSTATE 405; route numbers 101, 27, 134. W 61(CA) Signs: Yellow or White Background as per Note 4 (W61F(CA) and W61B(CA)). Callout: Down Vertical Arrow. No numbered notes on this sheet.
title: Route Shield Sizes and W61(CA) Signs
summary: Sizes of route shields used on overhead guide signs: 28 in. wide for U.S. and California shields with 1 or 2 digits, 32 in. for 3 digits, and Interstate shields 24 in. (1 or 2 digits) and 30 in. (3 digits). Also shows the W61F(CA) 84 in. by 20 in. and W61B(CA) 44 in. by 20 in. ONLY signs with 10 in. letters.

description:
Sheet 6 of 16 of S-418.6 with three schematic plan diagrams (not to scale, no dimensions) of arterial intersections using the fictitious street names Arden Boulevard, Beverly Drive, Clarita Avenue and Dolphin Street. Street edges are drawn as single lines, lane directions are shown with outlined arrows, raised islands are hatched, and sign locations are shown as a dot with a short double line and a letter. No sheet title text, dimensions or notes appear.

Top diagram (divergent arterial): Arden Boulevard comes in from the left as a two-way street (labels 'Arden' on the upper line and 'Boulevard' on the lower line) and splits at a long hatched triangular island into Beverly Drive, which curves up and to the right (labels 'Beverly' and 'Drive', two-way arrows), and Clarita Avenue, which continues straight to the right (labels 'Clarita' and 'Avenue', one arrow each way). A rightward arrow shows the through lane on the lower side of Arden Boulevard and diagonal arrows show the lanes entering Beverly Drive. Sign location A is marked on the lower edge of Arden Boulevard approach, left of the island.

Middle diagram (divergence with a cross street): The same Arden Boulevard, Beverly Drive and Clarita Avenue layout, with Dolphin Street added as a fourth leg going up and to the left from the center. The streets meet at a diamond-shaped central area with crosswalk lines. A hatched triangular island with a short stem sits at the bottom of the diamond next to Arden Boulevard and Clarita Avenue. Lane arrows are shown on each leg. Sign location A is marked on the lower line of the Arden Boulevard approach at the left and sign location B is marked on the upper side of Clarita Avenue on the right.

Bottom diagram (skewed multi-leg intersection): Arden Boulevard enters from the left (labels 'Arden' and 'Boulevard', arrows left and right), Beverly Drive runs vertically at the top and bottom (labels 'Drive' at top and 'Beverly' at bottom, up and down arrows), and Clarita Avenue approaches diagonally from the upper right (labels 'Clarita' and 'Avenue', arrows in both directions) with Boulevard continuing to the right. A multi-sided central intersection area is bounded by corner curb returns and two small hatched triangular islands on its upper-right side. Sign location C is marked on the lower line of the Arden Boulevard approach at the left, and sign location D is marked on Clarita Avenue near the upper right.
notes: No notes on this sheet. Labels shown: Arden Boulevard; Beverly Drive; Clarita Avenue; Dolphin Street; sign location letters A, B, C and D.
title: Overhead Guide Signing - Sign Location Diagrams A to D
summary: Three schematic intersection diagrams show example locations for overhead guide signs A through D: a divergent arterial where Arden Boulevard splits into Beverly Drive and Clarita Avenue, the same with Dolphin Street added, and a skewed multi-leg intersection. Lane arrows, hatched islands and sign location letters are shown but no dimensions.

description:
Sheet 7 of 16 of S-418.6: one large schematic plan (not to scale, no dimensions) of an example street network showing where overhead guide sign locations, each lettered, are placed. The sheet is drawn rotated, so streets labeled vertically read bottom to top. A north arrow at the right side points toward the top of the sheet. Street edges are single lines, break lines (squiggles) show roadways continuing beyond the sketch, outlined arrows show lane directions, and hatching is not used. Sign locations are drawn as a dot with a short double line and a letter.

Streets and labels shown: 'Street' (upper) and 'Upper' (lower) label the long left vertical street; 'Road' and 'Minor' label a second vertical roadway to its right; 'Lower' and 'Avenue' label the horizontal street crossing both; 'Suburban' and 'City Drive' label diagonal streets at the lower left; 'Boulevard' labels a horizontal street at the lower right; 'Golden State' and 'Fwy' with an Interstate 5 shield label the freeway running vertically on the right of the sheet; 'State' also appears beside the freeway ramps. The freeway is drawn as a double centerline with break lines.

Upper left area: the left vertical street (Upper Street) carries two-way arrows and has sign locations K and F on its upper stretch, and R, J, J and E on its lower stretch (E and J on the right-hand line, R on the left-hand line). Lower Avenue crosses it with a one-way arrow pair and a curved right-turn channel at the lower left. The vertical roadway to the right (Minor Road) has two-way arrows, signs U near its north end and S and T near the intersection with Lower Avenue, and sign Q on its northern curved portion. A diagonal X-shaped crossing of two streets is drawn at the top center.

East of those streets Lower Avenue runs east with signs L and G and flares into several lanes with a triangular island leading to the on and off ramps of the Golden State Fwy (Interstate 5) interchange. A partial cloverleaf with a loop ramp and ramp arrows is drawn on the east side of the freeway, with signs O and P on the cross street at the top right.

Lower right: a freeway interchange where Boulevard crosses the freeway on an overpass with ramps. Sign M is on the west approach, sign H is on the freeway overpass with 'H Alt.' marked beside it as an alternate location (with a leader arrow), sign I is on the overpass with 'I Alt.' marked as an alternate location on the east side, and sign N is on the east approach. At the lower left, Suburban and City Drive meet Minor Road in a skewed intersection with an arrow showing one-way flow on City Drive.
notes: No notes on this sheet. Labels shown: Street; Upper; Road; Minor; Lower; Avenue; Suburban; City Drive; Boulevard; Golden State; Fwy; State; Interstate 5 shield; north arrow; sign location letters E, F, G, H, H Alt., I, I Alt., J, K, L, M, N, O, P, Q, R, S, T, U.
title: Overhead Guide Signing - Sign Location Plan, Example Network
summary: Large schematic plan of an example street network around a freeway interchange, with overhead guide sign locations E through U (including H Alt. and I Alt.) placed on the approaches. It shows how the signs described on later sheets are located at divergences, left-turn lanes, ramps and cross streets. No dimensions or notes are given.

description:
Sheet 8 of 16 of S-418.6 showing sign layouts (no dimensions) for Sign A and Sign B. Each layout is a rectangular sign outline with legend, arrows and 'ONLY' boxes, with a caption at the right or below.

Sign A (3 approach lanes shown), four layout options for a divergence of Beverly Drive and Clarita Avenue. Layout 1: one panel with 'Beverly Drive' at the left over two bent diagonal (up-left) arrows with an 'ONLY' box between them, and 'Clarita Ave' at the right with a diagrammatic through-and-left arrow. Caption: 'See Notes 1~5. Diagrammatic Arrows shown due to optional lane, as per Note 3.' Layout 2: two panels separated by a vertical line. Left panel 'Beverly Drive' with two diagonal up-left arrows and an 'ONLY' box between them. Right panel 'Clarita Ave' with a vertical arrow and an 'ONLY' box. Caption: 'See Notes 1~5. Two-Line vertical and diagonal shown since optional lanes are not involved, as per Note 3.' Layout 3: 'Beverly Dr' over a bent arrow with an 'ONLY' box at left, a diagrammatic through-and-left arrow in the middle and 'Clarita Ave' over a vertical arrow with an 'ONLY' box at right. Caption: 'See Notes 1~5. Diagrammatic Arrows'. Layout 4: two panels separated by a vertical line. Left panel 'Beverly Dr' with an 'ONLY' box and a diagonal up-left arrow. Right panel 'Clarita Ave' with two vertical arrows and an 'ONLY' box between them. Caption: 'See Notes 1~5. Two-Line Arrows'.

Sign B (3 and 4 approach lanes shown), three layout options for Arden Blvd, Dolphin St and Beverly Dr. Layout 1: three stacked rows separated by horizontal lines: a left arrow with 'Arden Blvd', 'Dolphin St' with an up arrow, and 'Beverly Dr' with a right arrow. Caption: 'See Note 6. One-Line Arrows'. Layout 2: four panels separated by vertical lines: 'Arden Blvd' over two left-turn R3-5 type panels with 'ONLY', 'Dolphin St' over a straight-and-right arrow panel (R3-6), and 'Beverly Dr' over a right-turn panel with 'ONLY'. Caption: 'See Note 7. R3-5 and R3-6 shown, as per Note 7.' Layout 3: a left-turn 'ONLY' panel, 'Arden Blvd', another left-turn 'ONLY' panel, then two stacked rows 'Dolphin St' with an up arrow and 'Beverly Dr' with a right arrow. Caption: 'See Notes 6 and 7. One-Line Arrows'.
notes: Captions on the sheet: Sign A layout 1: See Notes 1~5. Diagrammatic Arrows shown due to optional lane, as per Note 3. Sign A layout 2: See Notes 1~5. Two-Line vertical and diagonal shown since optional lanes are not involved, as per Note 3. Sign A layout 3: See Notes 1~5. Diagrammatic Arrows. Sign A layout 4: See Notes 1~5. Two-Line Arrows. Sign B layout 1: See Note 6. One-Line Arrows. Sign B layout 2: See Note 7. R3-5 and R3-6 shown, as per Note 7. Sign B layout 3: See Notes 6 and 7. One-Line Arrows. The referenced Notes 1 to 7 are not on this sheet.
title: Overhead Guide Signing - Signs A and B Layouts
summary: Layout options for overhead Sign A (Beverly Drive and Clarita Ave, 3 approach lanes) using diagrammatic, Two-Line or ONLY arrows, and Sign B (Arden Blvd, Dolphin St and Beverly Dr, 3 and 4 approach lanes) using One-Line arrows or R3-5 and R3-6 panels. Each option is tied to notes on another sheet.

description:
Sheet 9 of 16 of S-418.6 showing sign layouts (no dimensions) for Signs C, D and E, with captions that refer to notes on another sheet.

Sign C (2 and more approach lanes): two layouts, each with a separate square regulatory sign at the left showing a no-left-turn symbol (left-turn arrow in a red circle with slash) with the plate 'ONTO BEVERLY DR'. Layout 1: a three-row guide sign with 'Clarita Ave' and an up-left diagonal arrow, 'Arden Blvd' with an up arrow, and 'Beverly Dr' with a right arrow. Caption: 'See Notes 6 and 8. One-Line Arrows'. Layout 2: a panel sequence of a bent up-left arrow with 'ONLY', a panel 'Clarita Ave', a second bent up-left arrow with 'ONLY', and two stacked rows 'Arden Blvd' with an up arrow and 'Beverly Dr' with a right arrow. Caption: 'See Notes 6, 7, 8 and 9. One-Line Arrows'.

Sign D (3 approach lanes shown): two layouts. Layout 1: three panels separated by vertical lines, headed 'Beverly Dr', 'Arden Blvd' and 'WEST' (large W, small EST). Each panel contains a lane-use arrow symbol: a left-and-through combination arrow with 'ONLY' under Beverly Dr, a right-turn arrow with 'ONLY' under Arden Blvd, and a through-and-right combination arrow under WEST. Caption: 'See Notes 7 and 9'. Layout 2: three panels separated by vertical lines: 'Arden Blvd EAST' with a left-turn arrow and 'ONLY', 'Beverly Dr SOUTH' with a bent up-left arrow and 'ONLY', and 'Arden Blvd WEST' with a three-way (left, through, right) arrow. The cardinal direction words have a large first letter. Caption: 'See Notes 7 and 9'.

Sign E: two layouts. Layout 1: a panel with a left arrow and 'Lower Ave'. Caption: 'See Notes 6. One-Line Arrow'. Layout 2: a panel with a left-turn arrow and 'ONLY' at the left and 'Lower Ave' at the right. Caption: 'See Notes 6 and 7'.
notes: Captions on the sheet: Sign C layout 1: See Notes 6 and 8. One-Line Arrows. Sign C layout 2: See Notes 6, 7, 8 and 9. One-Line Arrows. Sign D layout 1: See Notes 7 and 9. Sign D layout 2: See Notes 7 and 9. Sign E layout 1: See Notes 6. One-Line Arrow. Sign E layout 2: See Notes 6 and 7. Sign legends include ONTO BEVERLY DR, ONLY, WEST, EAST, SOUTH. The referenced Notes 6 to 9 are not on this sheet.
title: Overhead Guide Signing - Signs C, D and E Layouts
summary: Layout options for overhead Sign C (Clarita Ave, Arden Blvd and Beverly Dr with a no-left-turn ONTO BEVERLY DR sign), Sign D (lane-use symbol panels for Beverly Dr, Arden Blvd, WEST, EAST and SOUTH) and Sign E (Lower Ave with a left arrow or left-turn ONLY). Each option cites notes that are on another sheet.

description:
Sheet 10 of 16 of S-418.6 showing sign layouts (no dimensions) for Signs F, G and H, with captions that refer to notes on another sheet.

Sign F: two layouts. Layout 1: a panel with a left arrow at the left and 'To Lower Ave' stacked on three lines at the right. Caption: 'See Notes 6 and 10. One-Line Arrow'. Layout 2: a panel with a left-turn arrow and 'ONLY' at the left and 'To Lower Ave' at the right. Caption: 'See Notes 6, 7 and 10'.

Sign G (2 approach lanes shown): three layouts for Golden State Fwy. Each has a top row reading 'Golden State Fwy' with an Interstate 5 shield and a lower row split into NORTH and SOUTH halves. Layout 1: 'NORTH' with an up arrow and an 'ONLY' box on the left half, and an 'ONLY' box with an up-right diagonal arrow and 'SOUTH' on the right half, separated by a vertical line. Caption: 'See Notes 2, 3, 4, 5 and 11. Two-line Arrows'. Layout 2: an 'ONLY' box with an up arrow and 'NORTH' on the left, and a diagrammatic through-and-right arrow with 'SOUTH' on the right. Caption: 'See Notes 2, 3, 4, 5 and 11. Diagrammatic Arrows'. Layout 3: 'NORTH' with a diagrammatic through-and-right arrow on the left, and 'SOUTH' with a curved right arrow and an 'ONLY' box on the right. Caption: 'See notes 2, 3, 4, 5 and 11. Diagrammatic Arrows'.

Sign H: three entries. Layout 1: only the caption 'See Notes 6 and 11. One-Line Arrow' is shown, with no sign drawing beside it. Layout 2: a left-turn arrow with 'ONLY' at the left, and a panel with an Interstate 5 shield, 'Fwy', a left arrow and 'NORTH'. Caption: 'See Notes 7 and 11. One-Line Arrow'. Layout 3: a left-turn 'ONLY' panel, a center panel with an Interstate 5 shield, 'Fwy' and 'NORTH', and a second left-turn 'ONLY' panel. Caption: 'See Notes 7 and 11'.
notes: Captions on the sheet: Sign F layout 1: See Notes 6 and 10. One-Line Arrow. Sign F layout 2: See Notes 6, 7 and 10. Sign G layout 1: See Notes 2, 3, 4, 5 and 11. Two-line Arrows. Sign G layout 2: See Notes 2, 3, 4, 5 and 11. Diagrammatic Arrows. Sign G layout 3: See notes 2, 3, 4, 5 and 11. Diagrammatic Arrows. Sign H layout 1: See Notes 6 and 11. One-Line Arrow. Sign H layout 2: See Notes 7 and 11. One-Line Arrow. Sign H layout 3: See Notes 7 and 11. The referenced notes are not on this sheet.
title: Overhead Guide Signing - Signs F, G and H Layouts
summary: Layout options for overhead Sign F (To Lower Ave), Sign G (Golden State Fwy with an Interstate 5 shield and NORTH and SOUTH lane arrows, 2 approach lanes) and Sign H (Interstate 5 Fwy NORTH with left-turn ONLY panels). Each option cites notes that are on another sheet.

description:
Sheet 11 of 16 of S-418.6 showing sign layouts (no dimensions) for Sign H Alternate, Sign I and Sign I Alternate, with captions that refer to notes on another sheet.

Sign H Alternate: a two-tier sign. Top tier: an Interstate 5 shield and 'Fwy'. Bottom tier split into two halves: at the left an Advance arrow (bent, pointing left) with 'NORTH 300 FT', at the right 'SOUTH' with a right One-Line arrow. Caption: 'See Notes 11 and 12. Advance Arrow and One-Line Arrow'.

Sign I: three layouts. Layout 1: an Interstate 5 shield with 'Fwy' on the top line and a left arrow with 'SOUTH' on the second line. Caption: 'See Notes 6 and 11. One-Line Arrow'. Layout 2: a left-turn arrow with 'ONLY' at the left, and at the right a panel with the Interstate 5 shield, 'Fwy', a left arrow and 'SOUTH'. Caption: 'See Notes 7 and 11. One-Line Arrow'. Layout 3: three panels: a left-turn arrow with 'ONLY', a center panel with the Interstate 5 shield, 'Fwy' and 'SOUTH', and a diagrammatic through-and-left arrow panel. Caption: 'See Notes 7 and 11'.

Sign I Alternate: a two-tier sign. Top tier: an Interstate 5 shield and 'Freeway'. Bottom tier split into two halves: at the left an Advance arrow (bent, pointing left) with 'SOUTH 300 FT', at the right 'NORTH' with a right One-Line arrow. Caption: 'See Notes 11 and 12. Advance Arrow and One-Line Arrow'.
notes: Captions on the sheet: Sign H Alternate: See Notes 11 and 12. Advance Arrow and One-Line Arrow. Sign I layout 1: See Notes 6 and 11. One-Line Arrow. Sign I layout 2: See Notes 7 and 11. One-Line Arrow. Sign I layout 3: See Notes 7 and 11. Sign I Alternate: See Notes 11 and 12. Advance Arrow and One-Line Arrow. The referenced notes are not on this sheet.
title: Overhead Guide Signing - Signs H Alternate, I and I Alternate
summary: Layout options for overhead Sign I (Interstate 5 Fwy SOUTH with left arrow or left-turn ONLY panels) and the Alternate versions of Signs H and I, which show NORTH or SOUTH 300 FT with an Advance arrow and the opposite direction with a right arrow. Each cites notes that are on another sheet.

description:
Sheet 12 of 16 of S-418.6 showing sign layouts (no dimensions) for Sign J and Sign K, five layouts each, with captions that refer to notes on another sheet.

Sign J (legend 'Lower Ave'): Layout 1: 'Lower Ave' over a Down Vertical outline arrow. Caption: 'See Notes 13 and 14. Down Vertical Arrow'. Layout 2: 'Lower Ave' over a boxed solid down arrow with 'ONLY'. Caption: 'See Notes 13 and 14. Down Vertical Arrow for W61F sign, as per Note 14'. Layout 3: 'Lower Ave' over 'LEFT LANE'. Caption: 'See Notes 13 and 14'. Layout 4: 'Lower Ave' over 'NEXT LEFT'. Caption: 'See Notes 13, 14 and 15'. Layout 5: 'Lower Ave' over 'SECOND LEFT'. Caption: 'See Notes 13, 14 and 15'.

Sign K (legend 'To Lower Ave'): the same five layouts with 'To' added. Layout 1: 'To Lower Ave' over a Down Vertical outline arrow. Caption: 'See Notes 10, 13 and 14. Down Vertical Arrow'. Layout 2: 'To Lower Ave' over a boxed solid down arrow with 'ONLY'. Caption: 'See Notes 10, 13, 14 and 15. Down Vertical Arrow'. Layout 3: 'To Lower Ave' over 'LEFT LANE'. Caption: 'See Notes 10, 13 and 14'. Layout 4: 'To Lower Ave' over 'NEXT LEFT'. Caption: 'See Notes 10, 13 and 14'. Layout 5: 'To Lower Ave' over 'SECOND LEFT'. Caption: 'See Notes 10, 13 and 14'.
notes: Captions on the sheet: Sign J layout 1: See Notes 13 and 14. Down Vertical Arrow. Sign J layout 2: See Notes 13 and 14. Down Vertical Arrow for W61F sign, as per Note 14. Sign J layout 3: See Notes 13 and 14. Sign J layout 4: See Notes 13, 14 and 15. Sign J layout 5: See Notes 13, 14 and 15. Sign K layout 1: See Notes 10, 13 and 14. Down Vertical Arrow. Sign K layout 2: See Notes 10, 13, 14 and 15. Down Vertical Arrow. Sign K layout 3: See Notes 10, 13 and 14. Sign K layout 4: See Notes 10, 13 and 14. Sign K layout 5: See Notes 10, 13 and 14. The referenced notes are not on this sheet.
title: Overhead Guide Signing - Signs J and K Layouts
summary: Layout options for overhead Signs J (Lower Ave) and K (To Lower Ave), each with a Down Vertical arrow, a boxed down arrow with ONLY (W61F), LEFT LANE, NEXT LEFT and SECOND LEFT variations. Each option cites notes that are on another sheet.
